provider_query: Python standard library documentation for the venv module
answer:
Official and closely related sources for Python’s standard-library `venv` module:

1. **venv — Creation of virtual environments (current docs)** — Reference for the module: purpose, `python -m venv`, CLI flags, and the `EnvBuilder` API. Added in 3.3.  
   https://docs.python.org/3/library/venv.html

2. **venv — Python 3.14.1 library docs** — Same reference pinned to the 3.14 series (creation, isolation, `pyvenv.cfg`, API).  
   https://docs.python.org/3.14/library/venv.html

3. **Tutorial: Virtual Environments and Packages** — Official tutorial on creating and activating a venv (`.venv`, Windows vs Unix activation).  
   https://docs.python.org/3/tutorial/venv.html

4. **Tutorial source (venv.rst)** — ReStructuredText source of the virtual-environments tutorial in CPython.  
   https://raw.githubusercontent.com/python/cpython/HEAD/Doc/tutorial/venv.rst

5. **CPython `Lib/venv/__init__.py`** — Implementation of `EnvBuilder` and the `python -m venv` entry point (PEP 405).  
   https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/main/Lib/venv/__init__.py

6. **venv overview (pydevtools handbook)** — Short summary of stdlib `venv` (since 3.3), vs `virtualenv`/`uv`, and common flags such as `--upgrade-deps`.  
   https://pydevtools.com/handbook/reference/venv/

7. **Using a specific Python with stdlib venv** — How the interpreter you invoke selects the env’s Python (`python3.x -m venv`), plus the common “No module named venv” case on minimal Linux installs.  
   https://www.pythontutorials.net/blog/how-do-i-use-different-python-version-in-venv-from-standard-library-not-virtualenv/

8. **Create, activate, deactivate, delete (Python Land)** — Practical walkthrough of `python -m venv` and the resulting directory layout, with a link back to the official docs.  
   https://python.land/virtual-environments/virtualenv
